world.h: Yemen's government opens major Houthi offensive
world.b: Rashad al-Alimi, head of Yemen's presidential leadership council, announced major military operations to retake Houthi-held territory.
more: Government forces say they took the Dhubab district near the Bab al-Mandeb strait, west of Taiz.
Iran said there is no military solution to its conflict with the United States.

world.h: Ethiopian forces retake Tigray capital Mekelle
world.b: Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters captured Mekelle after the TPLF withdrew from the city on Saturday.
more: Eritrea cut diplomatic ties after Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats.
Explosions were reported in Addis Ababa, including near the military headquarters.

world.h: Four leaders call for peace as Ethiopia war grows
world.b: The leaders of Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan met in New Alamein City and called for political and peaceful solutions to regional conflicts.
more: They said control of the Red Sea should stay with coastal states, opposing landlocked Ethiopia's push for sea access.

world.h: Iran: Hormuz stays shut until US meets 7 conditions
world.b: Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz will not open until Tehran's seven conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum are met.
more: The strait has been blocked for more than seven months since US-Israel strikes on February 28.
About one-fifth of the world's oil and gas shipping passes through the strait in peacetime.

world.h: Air strike in Sudan kills UN food aid driver
world.b: The World Food Programme said a driver was killed when an air strike hit a convoy of trucks clearly marked as humanitarian vehicles in South Kordofan state.
more: The WFP called for an investigation but did not say who was responsible.
Sudan's war has displaced 14 million people, and 19.5 million face acute food insecurity.

world.h: OPEC+ keeps oil output steady for November
world.b: Seven OPEC+ members including Saudi Arabia and Russia agreed to keep oil production unchanged for November.
more: The G7 separately announced plans to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products.
Brent crude has been trading above $100 a barrel and US diesel prices have hit record highs.

world.h: US pulls B-1 bombers from UK's RAF Fairford
world.b: The Pentagon said all US bombers deployed to RAF Fairford in England have returned to their home stations as a precaution, after arrests over alleged plots against the base.
more: On October 2, British police arrested a 25-year-old UK-Iranian dual national on suspicion of plotting an attack on the base.
Iran has denied involvement and summoned the UK ambassador.

world.h: Zelenskyy says Ukraine ready for US-backed talks
world.b: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready for three-way talks with the US and Russia, with technical-level talks possible by the end of the month.
more: Possible venues include the United Arab Emirates or another place proposed by Washington.
India said it plans to increase its mediation role, including on Black Sea shipping and grain exports.

world.b: Australian authorities are investigating the ties of Hamam al-Hammami, the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking his captain with an axe on Flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30.
more: The Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight diverted safely to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where a reserve pilot landed it.
Al-Hammami had been barred from flying in Oman over extremism concerns and reportedly studied in Melbourne about a decade ago.

national.h: Search ends for six aboard crashed medical jet
national.b: The Coast Guard suspended its search for six people aboard a Gulfstream G100 medical flight from Bermuda to Boston.
more: Crews searched about 66 hours over 4,445 miles and found debris off Nantucket.
The crew of four were Canadian; the patient and a relative were from Bermuda.

national.h: Christa Pike still unconscious after failed execution
national.b: Christa Pike's lawyer said she has not regained consciousness since Tennessee's failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection on Wednesday.
more: Pike, 50, remains hospitalized on a ventilator under guard.
Tennessee prisons commissioner Frank Strada resigned Saturday, and Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent investigation.

national.h: Cornell president vows transparency in rape case
national.b: Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff called an alleged 2024 gang rape at the Chi Phi fraternity "deeply disturbing" and pledged an independent review.
more: The alleged victim has sued the university and seven former students.
Governor Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in the case.

national.h: Judge rules activist Salah Sarsour can be deported
national.b: A US judge ruled that Palestinian rights advocate Salah Sarsour, who has lived in the US for more than 30 years, can be deported under a Cold War-era law.
more: The government says he poses a threat to American foreign policy.

national.h: Mamdani and Irish PM ride the G train
national.b: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin rode the G train referencing the "Split the G" Guinness trend and played bingo at the New York Irish Center.
more: The outings took place during UN week in September; Al Jazeera published the video on October 4.

politics.h: Trump predicts 'big surprise' at Ohio rally
politics.b: President Trump held a rally at Butler High School in Vandalia, Ohio, backing Senator Jon Husted against Democrat Sherrod Brown and urging supporters to vote.
more: Trump said, "Just get out and vote. If you do that, we're going to win, and we're going to win big."
Ohio gas prices are up 35% from a year ago at $4.16 a gallon, Al Jazeera reported.

politics.h: Cornell case spurs push to change NY rape laws
politics.b: New York lawmakers are pressing bills to close the state's "voluntary intoxication" distinction in sexual assault law, which passed the state Senate in June and awaits an Assembly vote.
more: Other bills would extend rape-shield protections to civil cases and protect people who report sexual assault from defamation suits.
Governor Kathy Hochul said, "Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape. Period."

politics.h: KKK leader claims rising support before midterms
politics.b: A Ku Klux Klan leader told Al Jazeera's Phil Lavelle that support for the group's message is growing ahead of the midterm elections.
more: The group is trying to rebrand itself around "family and faith," and the report examines its actual influence.

politics.h: UK Greens vote to define Zionism as racism
politics.b: Britain's Green Party voted 1,022 to 813 at its Brighton conference to define Zionism as an ethnonationalist political project and a form of racism.
more: Israeli President Isaac Herzog called the vote "a disgrace and a shame."
Party leader Zack Polanski did not vote on the motion.

politics.h: Spain protests after housing decrees rejected
politics.b: Spain's parliament rejected two government decrees meant to protect renters and limit short-term leases, and tens of thousands protested nationwide on Saturday.
more: Opposition leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo called for immediate elections.
A snap election could come as early as November 29.

international.h: Brazil heads to Lula-Bolsonaro run-off Oct 25
international.b: Flavio Bolsonaro won 47% of valid votes to President Lula's 44.9%, so neither won outright.
more: Bolsonaro got about 56 million votes to Lula's nearly 53 million.
Bolsonaro's Liberal Party is set to become the largest party in the Chamber of Deputies.

international.h: Malaysia sends 1,479 people back to Myanmar
international.b: Two navy warships and a hospital ship carrying 1,479 Myanmar refugees and migrants arrived in Yangon early Sunday.
more: Malaysia plans to send back 5,000 in this first phase; more than 10,300 others are held in its detention centres.
The UN refugee agency said staff could not confirm the returns were genuinely free and informed.

international.h: Singapore turns matchmaker as births hit low
international.b: Fewer than 30,000 babies were born in Singapore in 2025, a fertility rate of 0.87.
more: The government gives about S$70,000 ($55,000) in benefits per child from birth to age 17.

international.h: Nicaragua to quit Central American Parliament
international.b: Nicaragua's Foreign Ministry said it will withdraw from the regional parliament.
more: The government left the OAS in 2023 and the UN Human Rights Council in 2025 after criticism of its rights record.

international.h: Early Bosnia results show familiar parties ahead
international.b: Early results in Bosnia's general election showed Denis Becirovic, Zeljka Cvijanovic and Darijana Filipovic leading for the three seats of the presidency.
more: About 3.4 million people were eligible to vote.
It was the first nationwide use of fingerprint identification and electronic ballot scanners.

international.h: Russia hits Kyiv bridge during Merz visit
international.b: Russia struck the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River in Kyiv on Sunday while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz was visiting the city.
more: Merz announced a $1.1 billion military aid package and $394 million for energy repairs.
He said, "If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us."

international.h: France to close up to 500 schools amid protests
international.b: France's education ministry said 400 to 500 schools will close Monday as student protests over staffing and class hours have turned violent.
more: Since the protests began, 24 schools have been burned or ransacked and more than 5,000 people were arrested in the past week.
Organizers plan to resume demonstrations Tuesday.

sports.b: Keelon Russell threw for 285 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another score.
Michigan's Bryce Underwood completed 10 of 21 passes for 101 yards with two interceptions.
Northwestern outrushed Penn State 413 yards to 48.
Drake Maye threw for 269 yards and three touchdowns and ran for 54 yards as New England beat Buffalo.
more: Maye led a game-winning 73-yard drive that included a 23-yard touchdown pass to Efton Chism.

sports.h: Lamb's 17 catches lift Cowboys past Texans 34-30
sports.b: CeeDee Lamb caught 17 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown in Dallas's win over Houston.
more: Dak Prescott hit Lamb for the game-winning 12-yard score with 40 seconds remaining.

sports.b: Matthew Stafford completed 13 of 17 passes for 149 yards in the fourth quarter as Los Angeles beat Philadelphia.
more: Puka Nacua caught five passes for 76 yards in the final quarter alone.
Philadelphia went 0-for-12 on third-down attempts.

sports.b: Emanuel Wilson scored twice, on a 23-yard catch and an 8-yard run, as Seattle beat the Chargers.
more: Wilson ran for 81 yards on 21 carries.
Seattle was called for 14 penalties for a franchise-record 150 yards.

sports.b: San Francisco beat Denver to remain undefeated.
more: The 49ers have not allowed a sack through four games.

sports.b: Kyle Monangai rushed for 146 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries as Chicago beat New York.
more: The Bears totaled 232 rushing yards and held the Jets without a third-down conversion.

sports.h: Chourio walk-off puts Brewers up 2-0 on Padres
sports.b: Milwaukee beat San Diego 4-3 in NLDS Game 2 on Jackson Chourio's two-run single in the ninth inning.
more: The Brewers drew three walks against Padres closer Mason Miller before Chourio's hit.
Milwaukee leads the series 2-0.

sports.h: Rasmussen, Rays blank Yankees 1-0 in Game 1
sports.b: Drew Rasmussen struck out 10 and carried a no-hitter into the eighth inning as Tampa Bay beat New York.
more: Yankees catcher Austin Wells was thrown out at third trying to stretch a double into a triple in the eighth.
Tampa Bay leads the Division Series 1-0.

goodnews.h: Man catches child who fell from balcony in Egypt
goodnews.b: Video shows a man in Egypt rushing to catch a young boy who fell from a second-floor balcony.
more: The child hit a washing line on the way down, giving the man crucial extra time to reach him.

goodnews.h: Dakar neighbours clean up school for new year
goodnews.b: Students, teachers and volunteers in Dakar, Senegal, cleaned Medina Gounass Elementary School on Saturday ahead of the new academic year.
more: They swept classrooms, cleared drains and removed plastic and household waste.
Organizers said the effort also aimed to raise awareness about protecting the environment.

local.h: Sixth person dies after falling ill in NYPD custody
local.b: Reginald Newkirk, 54, of Brooklyn died Sunday at Kings County Hospital, at least the sixth person this year to die after a medical crisis in NYPD custody.
more: He was arrested Friday for drug possession, hospitalized and cleared, then had another medical emergency Saturday afternoon.
Public defenders have called for independent Civilian Complaint Review Board investigations of every death in police custody.

local.h: NY prison system staffing crisis drives workers away
local.b: New York's prison system has a 56% vacancy rate among corrections workers.
more: New officer training is up 40%, but more than 250 of 660 newly trained officers resigned within a year.
The state spent over $1 billion deploying the National Guard after about 2,000 guards were fired following a 2025 wildcat strike.

local.h: NJ reports first West Nile Virus death of the year
local.b: New Jersey reported its first West Nile Virus death of 2026, a South Jersey resident over 60.
more: As of Thursday the state had confirmed 26 cases, 19 with neurological illness, already above last year's total of 23.

local.h: Banned books and Winnie the Pooh in NYC libraries
local.b: City library branches have a busy October, including banned-book events and NYPL celebrations of Winnie the Pooh's 100th birthday.
more: Queens Public Library and Penguin Random House are holding a banned book giveaway at the Hunters Point branch.

periods.name: Monday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 69. Breezy, with a northwest wind 9 to 14 mph increasing to 16 to 21 mph in the afternoon.

periods.name: Monday Night
periods.text: Clear, with a low around 50. Northwest wind 13 to 15 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 63. Northwest wind 9 to 11 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday Night
periods.text: Clear, with a low around 50. West wind 3 to 7 mph.

periods.name: Wednesday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 56.

localgood.h: Banned books and Pooh at NYC libraries
localgood.b: NYC libraries mark Banned Books Week this October, with Queens Public Library offering free banned titles.
more: NYPL is celebrating Winnie the Pooh's centennial with movies, readings and crafts across the boroughs.
